items.name: Commit Multiple Files
items.description: Tool to atomically create, update, or delete multiple files in a GitHub repository as a single commit. Uses Git Data APIs to avoid SHA mismatch conflicts that occur with the Contents API when multiple files are modified in parallel. Use when you need to make multi-file changes reliably. BRANCH CREATION: When committing to a new branch (e.g., 'fix/my-fix' or 'feature/new-feature'), you MUST provide 'base_branch' (typically 'main' or 'master') to create the branch from. If the branch already exists, base_branch is not needed. This action handles race conditions automatically: if the branch is updated by another commit between fetching the HEAD and updating the reference (resulting in a 422 'not a fast forward' error), the action will retry by refetching the HEAD and rebasing changes. Use max_retries to control this behavior.

repo.title: Repo

repo.human_parameter_description: The repository you want to deploy from (just the name, no .git). This identifies the specific project.

task.title: Task
task.description: Specifies a task to execute, e.g., `deploy` or `deploy:migrations`.
task.human_parameter_description: What command your deployment workflow should run, like 'deploy' or 'deploy:migrations'. Choose the task that matches how you deploy.

owner.title: Owner
owner.description: The account owner of the repository. This name is not case-sensitive. The repository must exist and the authenticated user must have access to it.
owner.human_parameter_description: The GitHub username or organization that owns the repository you want to deploy from. This tells us where the repo lives.

payload.title: Payload
payload.description: A JSON string payload providing additional information that a deployment system might need, customizable based on the deployment process.
payload.human_parameter_description: Optional JSON with extra details your deployment system needs (for example, target server, feature flags, or run options). Only include if your process expects it.

auto_merge.title: Auto Merge
auto_merge.description: Attempts to automatically merge the default branch into the requested ref if the ref is behind the default branch. Set to `false` to disable.
auto_merge.human_parameter_description: If enabled, we'll try to merge the default branch into your chosen ref before deploying so it's up to date. Disable to deploy exactly what's on the ref.

description.title: Description
examples: Deploying new feature X to staging.
description.description: A short description of the deployment. Maximum length of 1000 characters.
description.human_parameter_description: A short note explaining what this deployment is for, so teammates understand the change.

environment.title: Environment

required_contexts.title: Required Contexts

required_contexts.human_parameter_description: Which status checks must pass before creating the deployment. Leave empty ([]) to bypass checks, or omit to require all available checks.

owner.title: Owner

items.name: Create a deployment status
items.description: Creates a status for an existing deployment, updating its operational state, associated URLs, and description.

input_parameters.title: CreateADeploymentStatusRequest

repo.title: Repo
repo.description: The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.
repo.human_parameter_description: The name of the repository under the specified account (no .git). This identifies where to create the deployment status.

owner.title: Owner
owner.description: The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.
owner.human_parameter_description: The username or organization that owns the repository. This tells us which account the repository belongs to.

state.title: State
state.description: State of the status. Setting a transient deployment to `inactive` shows it as `destroyed` in GitHub.
state.human_parameter_description: How this deployment is currently doing (for example, success, pending, or failure). Choose the option that best reflects the latest result.

log_url.title: Log Url
log_url.description: URL for deployment output. Preferred over `target_url`; setting this also sets `target_url` to the same value.
log_url.human_parameter_description: A direct link to the build or deployment logs so others can review what happened. If set, this will also be used as the target URL.

target_url.title: Target Url
target_url.description: URL for deployment status updates or output. `log_url` is generally preferred.
target_url.human_parameter_description: A link people can follow to see more details about this deployment’s status or output. If you also provide a log URL, that will be used instead.

description.title: Description
description.description: Short description of the status (max 140 characters).
description.human_parameter_description: A brief note explaining what happened in this deployment. Keep it short and clear for teammates.

environment.title: Environment
environment.description: Name for the target deployment environment (e.g., `production`, `staging`). If unset, uses environment from previous status or deployment.
environment.human_parameter_description: Where this deployment is running, like production or staging. This helps readers understand which environment the status applies to.

auto_inactive.title: Auto Inactive
auto_inactive.description: If true, sets prior successful, non-transient, non-production deployments in the same repository and environment to `inactive`.
auto_inactive.human_parameter_description: Turn this on to automatically mark older successful deployments in the same environment as inactive. It keeps the environment focused on the newest deployment.

deployment_id.title: Deployment Id
deployment_id.description: The unique identifier of the deployment for which to create a status.
deployment_id.human_parameter_description: The specific deployment you want to update. You can get this ID from when the deployment was created or from a list of deployments.

environment_url.title: Environment Url
environment_url.description: URL for accessing the target deployment environment.
environment_url.human_parameter_description: A link to the live environment for this deployment, such as your staging or production site. This helps others quickly verify the result.

items.name: Create a github pages deployment

repo.human_parameter_description: The name of the repository you want to deploy. Use the short name (without .git) so we can find the correct project.

owner.title: Owner
owner.description: The account owner of the repository (e.g., a GitHub username or organization name). This field is not case-sensitive.
owner.human_parameter_description: The GitHub username or organization that owns the repository you want to deploy from. This tells us which account to look in.

oidc_token.title: Oidc Token
oidc_token.description: OIDC token from GitHub Actions for deployment authorization, typically from `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` with `id-token: write` permission.
oidc_token.human_parameter_description: The OIDC token from your GitHub Actions run that authorizes this deployment. This lets GitHub verify the workflow and allow the Pages publish.

artifact_id.title: Artifact Id
artifact_id.description: Identifier of a GitHub Actions artifact (e.g., .zip or .tar) with static assets for deployment. Artifact must belong to the repository. Either this or `artifact_url` is required.
artifact_id.human_parameter_description: The numeric ID of the Actions artifact that contains your built site files to publish. Provide this if you know the artifact ID; otherwise use Artifact URL.

environment.title: Environment
environment.description: Target environment for this GitHub Pages deployment. Defaults to `github-pages`.
environment.human_parameter_description: The environment you want to deploy to, such as 'github-pages' or 'production'. This helps label and track where your site is published.

items.name: Create an autolink reference for a repository
items.description: Creates a repository autolink to automatically convert text references (e.g., 'TICKET-123') into hyperlinks, using a unique `key_prefix` and a `url_template` that includes `<num>`.

input_parameters.title: CreateAnAutolinkReferenceForARepositoryRequest

repo.title: Repo
repo.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. The name is not case-sensitive.
repo.human_parameter_description: The repository where you want to create the autolink. Use the exact repo name as it appears on GitHub (without .git).

owner.title: Owner
owner.description: The account owner of the repository. This can be a username or an organization name. The name is not case-sensitive.
owner.human_parameter_description: Who owns the repository you want to add the autolink to. Enter the GitHub username or organization name.

key_prefix.title: Key Prefix
key_prefix.description: Prefix that triggers the autolink (e.g., 'JIRA-'). When followed by an identifier, it's converted into a link. Must be non-empty and not contain spaces.
key_prefix.human_parameter_description: The short code that triggers the link, like 'JIRA-' or 'TICKET-'. When text starts with this prefix followed by an ID, it will be turned into a clickable link.

url_template.title: Url Template
url_template.description: URL template for the autolink, using `<num>` as a placeholder for the reference identifier (e.g., 'https://example.atlassian.net/browse/<num>'). Behavior of `<num>` is determined by `is_alphanumeric`.
url_template.human_parameter_description: The web address pattern to open when the prefix and number are detected. Put <num> where the issue or ticket number should go (for example, https://example.atlassian.net/browse/<num>).

is_alphanumeric.title: Is Alphanumeric
is_alphanumeric.description: Specifies if the `<num>` placeholder in `url_template` matches alphanumeric characters (`A-Z` (case-insensitive), `0-9`, and `-`) or only numeric characters (`0-9`).
is_alphanumeric.human_parameter_description: Choose whether the <num> part can include letters as well as numbers (A-Z, 0-9, and -) or only numbers. Turn this on for IDs like 'ABC-123'; turn it off for purely numeric IDs.

items.name: Create an organization webhook
items.description: Creates a webhook for a GitHub organization to deliver event notifications to a configured URL.

input_parameters.title: CreateAnOrganizationWebhookRequest

org.title: Org
org.description: The name of the GitHub organization. This name is not case-sensitive.
org.human_parameter_description: The GitHub organization you want to add the webhook to. Enter the org's name as it appears in the URL on GitHub.

name.title: Name
name.description: The name of the webhook. Must be "web" for organization webhooks. Defaults to "web".
name.human_parameter_description: The kind of webhook you're creating. For organization webhooks, this must be 'web'. Defaults to 'web'.

active.title: Active
active.description: Boolean indicating if the webhook is active. `true` sends notifications, `false` does not. Defaults to `true`.
active.human_parameter_description: Turn delivery on or off. Set to true to start receiving events right away, or false to create the webhook without sending notifications.

events.title: Events
events.description: List of event names to trigger the webhook. Use `['*']` for all events. Defaults to `['push']` if not specified. See GitHub docs for event types.
events.human_parameter_description: Which organization events should trigger this webhook. Use '*' for all events or list specific ones like 'push' or 'issues'.

config__url.title: Config  Url
config__url.description: Required. The target URL for webhook payload delivery. This URL is a mandatory part of the webhook's `config` object and will receive POST requests for subscribed events.
config__url.human_parameter_description: The endpoint on your server where GitHub should deliver event notifications. Use a publicly reachable HTTPS URL that can receive POST requests.

config__secret.title: Config  Secret
config__secret.description: Optional secret for generating an HMAC hex digest for payload verification (X-Hub-Signature-256 header). If provided, this is used as the key.
config__secret.human_parameter_description: A shared secret used to verify that webhook payloads are really from GitHub. Save this value in your service to validate incoming requests.

config__password.title: Config  Password
config__password.description: Password for basic authentication if the webhook endpoint (`config_url`) requires it, corresponding to `config_username`.
config__password.human_parameter_description: Provide the password that matches the username if your webhook endpoint uses basic authentication.

config__username.title: Config  Username
config__username.description: Username for basic authentication if the webhook endpoint (`config_url`) requires it. Use only if your endpoint is protected by basic auth.
config__username.human_parameter_description: Provide a username only if your webhook endpoint requires basic authentication.

config__content__type.title: Config  Content  Type
config__content__type.description: The media type for serializing webhook payloads. Supported: `json`, `form`. GitHub API defaults to `form` if this field is not set or is `None`.
config__content__type.human_parameter_description: Choose how you want the webhook payload to be formatted—'json' is easiest for most services; 'form' sends data as form-encoded.

config__insecure__ssl.title: Config  Insecure  Ssl
config__insecure__ssl.description: Controls SSL certificate verification for `config_url`. '1' disables verification (not recommended), '0' enables. GitHub API defaults to '0' (verification enabled) if this field is not set or is `None`.
config__insecure__ssl.human_parameter_description: Whether to skip SSL certificate checks for the webhook URL. Use '0' to verify (recommended) or '1' to skip verification for self-signed certs.

items.name: Create a pull request
items.description: Creates a pull request in a GitHub repository, requiring existing `base` and `head` branches; `title` or `issue` must be provided.

input_parameters.title: CreateAPullRequestRequest

base.title: Base
base.description: The name of the branch you want the changes pulled into. This must be an existing branch on the current (target) repository. You cannot submit a pull request to one repository that requests a merge to a base branch of another repository.
base.human_parameter_description: The branch you want to merge your changes into, usually 'main' or 'develop'. Choose a branch that already exists in the target repository.

body.title: Body
examples: This PR introduces a new feature that does X, Y, and Z.
Fixes #42 by addressing the off-by-one error.
body.description: The detailed description or contents of the pull request.
body.human_parameter_description: Explain what this pull request changes and why. Include any context, screenshots, or links that help reviewers.

head.title: Head
head.description: The name of the branch where your changes are implemented. IMPORTANT: This branch must already exist in the repository (or fork) before calling this action. You must first create the branch and push commits to it (using git or the 'Create a reference' action), then create the PR. For cross-repository pull requests, namespace `head` with the source owner and branch, like `username:branch`.
head.human_parameter_description: The source branch that contains your changes. CRITICAL: This branch must already exist in the repository before you can create a pull request. The typical workflow is: 1) Create a new branch, 2) Push commits to that branch, 3) Then create a PR. If the branch is in a fork or another repository, use the format owner:branch.

repo.title: Repo
repo.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This name is not case-sensitive.
repo.human_parameter_description: The repository name where you want to create the pull request. Use the short name like 'Spoon-Knife' (no .git).

draft.title: Draft
draft.description: Indicates whether the pull request should be created as a draft. Draft pull requests cannot be merged until marked as ready for review.
draft.human_parameter_description: Create the pull request as a draft to get early feedback before it's ready to merge. Drafts can't be merged until you mark them ready for review.

issue.title: Issue
issue.description: The number of an existing issue in the repository to convert into a pull request. If provided, the issue's title and body may be used for the pull request. Required if `title` is not specified.
issue.human_parameter_description: If you want to turn an existing issue into a pull request, enter its issue number. When provided, the pull request can reuse the issue's title and description.

owner.title: Owner
owner.description: The account owner of the repository. This name is not case-sensitive.
owner.human_parameter_description: The username or organization that owns the repository where you want to open the pull request. Use the exact account name as it appears on GitHub.

title.title: Title

title.human_parameter_description: A short, clear headline for your pull request so reviewers know what it does. Skip this if you're converting an existing issue.

head_repo.title: Head Repo
head_repo.description: The name of the repository (e.g., 'octocat/Hello-World') where the changes in the pull request were made. This field is required for cross-repository pull requests if both the source and target repositories are owned by the same organization but are different repositories.

maintainer_can_modify.description: Indicates whether maintainers of the upstream repository can modify the pull request. This is primarily relevant for pull requests originating from forks.
maintainer_can_modify.human_parameter_description: Allow repository maintainers to push commits to your pull request. Turn this on if you want maintainers to help polish or fix your branch.

items.name: Create a repository ruleset
items.description: Creates a uniquely named ruleset for a repository, defining rules for branches or tags with specified enforcement, conditions, and bypass actors.

input_parameters.title: CreateARepositoryRulesetRequest

name.title: Name
name.human_parameter_description: A unique, friendly name for this ruleset. Pick something that clearly describes what the ruleset is for.

repo.title: Repo
repo.description: Name of the repository, without the `.git` extension (not case-sensitive).
repo.human_parameter_description: The short name of the repository where you want to add the ruleset. Use the name as shown on GitHub (without .git).

owner.title: Owner
owner.description: Account owner of the repository (not case-sensitive).
owner.human_parameter_description: The username or organization that owns the repository. This identifies where to create the ruleset.

rules.title: Rules
rules.description: Array of rule objects as a JSON string to be enforced. Each must have `type` and may have `parameters`. Refer to GitHub API docs for available rule types and parameters. Example: '[{"type": "creation"}, {"type": "deletion"}]'
rules.human_parameter_description: The protections you want to apply as a JSON string. Choose the rule types you need and, if needed, provide their settings.

target.title: TargetEnm
target.description: The target of the ruleset, whether it applies to branches or tags.
target.human_parameter_description: Choose whether these rules apply to branches or tags in this repository so GitHub knows where to enforce them.

enforcement.title: Enforcement
enforcement.description: Enforcement level: `disabled` (ruleset is not enforced), `active` (ruleset is enforced), or `evaluate` (test rules before enforcing; GitHub Enterprise only).
enforcement.human_parameter_description: How strictly to apply the rules: turn them off, enforce them, or evaluate them to test without blocking changes.

bypass_actors.title: Bypass Actors
bypass_actors.description: Actors that can bypass rules in this ruleset as a JSON string. Each actor object requires `actor_id`, `actor_type` (e.g., 'Team', 'Integration'), and `bypass_mode` (e.g., 'always'). Example: '[{"actor_id": 1, "actor_type": "Team", "bypass_mode": "always"}]'
bypass_actors.human_parameter_description: Who is allowed to bypass these rules as a JSON string. Use this to grant exceptions to trusted users, teams, or apps (like CI).

conditions__ref__name__exclude.title: Conditions  Ref  Name  Exclude
conditions__ref__name__exclude.description: Ref names or patterns to exclude. Condition fails if any pattern matches the ref name.
conditions__ref__name__exclude.human_parameter_description: Branches or tags to exclude from this ruleset. Use names or patterns to carve out exceptions where the rules should not apply.

conditions__ref__name__include.title: Conditions  Ref  Name  Include
conditions__ref__name__include.description: Ref names/patterns to include. Condition passes if one pattern matches the ref name. Use `~DEFAULT_BRANCH` for default branch, `~ALL` for all branches.
conditions__ref__name__include.human_parameter_description: Which branches or tags this ruleset should include. Add exact names or simple patterns (like feature-*) to target the refs you care about.

items.name: Create a review comment for a pull request
items.description: Creates a review comment on a pull request's diff, targeting a specific line, range of lines, an entire file, or replying to an existing comment.

input_parameters.title: CreateAReviewCommentForAPullRequestRequest

body.title: Body
body.description: Text content of the review comment.
body.human_parameter_description: What you want to say in the review comment. Write clear feedback for the code author.

line.title: Line
line.description: **[LINE-BASED MODE]** Line number in the diff for the comment. Required when using line-based mode (must be used with `side`). For multi-line comments, this is the last line of the range. Do not use with position or in_reply_to parameters.
line.human_parameter_description: The line number in the diff where you want to place the comment. For multi-line comments, set this to the last line of the range.

path.title: Path
path.description: Relative path of the file for the comment.
path.human_parameter_description: The file path in the repository where you want to leave the comment. Use the relative path shown in the pull request (e.g., 'src/main.py').

repo.title: Repo
repo.description: Repository name without the `.git` extension (not case sensitive).
repo.human_parameter_description: The repository name where the pull request lives. Don't include '.git'.

side.title: SideEnm
side.description: **[LINE-BASED MODE]** Side of the diff (`LEFT` or `RIGHT`) for the comment. Required when using line-based mode with the `line` parameter. For multi-line comments, refers to the last line of the range. Do not use with position or in_reply_to parameters. **IMPORTANT:** Use `LEFT` only for deletions that appear in red in the diff. Use `RIGHT` for additions (green) or unchanged context lines (white). Attempting to comment on LEFT side lines that are not visible deletions in the diff will result in a 'could not be resolved' error.
side.human_parameter_description: Which side of the split diff you're commenting on: 'LEFT' for deleted lines (red) or 'RIGHT' for added/unchanged lines (green/white). LEFT can ONLY be used for lines that appear as deletions in the diff.

owner.title: Owner
owner.description: Account owner of the repository (not case sensitive).
owner.human_parameter_description: The username or organization that owns the repository you want to comment in. Enter the account name, for example 'octocat'.

position.title: Position
position.description: **[DEPRECATED - Use line-based mode instead]** Position in the diff hunk for the comment. When using position mode, do not provide line, side, start_line, start_side, or in_reply_to parameters.
position.human_parameter_description: Where in the diff the comment should appear. Prefer using 'line' instead; this is mainly for older workflows.

commit_id.title: Commit Id
commit_id.description: SHA of the commit for the comment. Using an outdated `commit_id` can misplace the comment if lines change.
commit_id.human_parameter_description: The exact commit your comment should attach to. This helps ensure your comment lines up with the version of the code you reviewed.

start_line.title: Start Line
start_line.description: **[LINE-BASED MODE - MULTI-LINE]** First line in the diff for a multi-line comment. Required when creating a multi-line comment (must be used with `start_side`, `line`, and `side`). Do not use with position or in_reply_to parameters.
start_line.human_parameter_description: The first line in the diff for a multi-line comment. Use this together with 'line' to define the full range.

start_side.title: StartSideEnm
start_side.description: **[LINE-BASED MODE - MULTI-LINE]** Starting side of the diff (`LEFT` or `RIGHT`) for a multi-line comment. Required when creating a multi-line comment (must be used with `start_line`, `line`, and `side`). Do not use with position or in_reply_to parameters. **IMPORTANT:** Use `LEFT` only for deletions that appear in red in the diff. Use `RIGHT` for additions (green) or unchanged context lines (white). Attempting to use LEFT for lines that are not visible deletions will result in a 'could not be resolved' error.
start_side.human_parameter_description: Which side of the diff the first line of your multi-line comment is on. 'LEFT' can ONLY be used for lines that appear as deletions (red) in the diff. Use 'RIGHT' for added or unchanged lines.

in_reply_to.title: In Reply To
in_reply_to.description: **[REPLY MODE]** ID of an existing review comment to reply to. When using reply mode, do not provide position, line, side, start_line, or start_side parameters as they will be ignored.
in_reply_to.human_parameter_description: The ID of an existing review comment you want to reply to. Use this when continuing a conversation instead of starting a new comment.

pull_number.title: Pull Number
pull_number.description: Identifier of the pull request.
pull_number.human_parameter_description: The pull request number you want to comment on. You can find this number in the PR's title or URL.

items.name: Create a dependency snapshot
items.description: Creates a snapshot of a repository's dependencies to populate the GitHub dependency graph and enable security alerts; `sha` must be a 40-character commit ID, `ref` a fully qualified Git reference (e.g., `refs/heads/main`), and `scanned` an ISO 8601 timestamp.

input_parameters.title: CreateASnapshotOfDependenciesForARepositoryRequest

ref.title: Ref
ref.description: Git reference (fully qualified, e.g., `refs/heads/main`) of the repository branch/tag that triggered this snapshot.
ref.human_parameter_description: The branch or tag ref that triggered the snapshot, like refs/heads/main or refs/tags/v1.0. This ties the snapshot to a specific ref.

sha.title: Sha
sha.description: Commit SHA (maximum 40 characters) associated with this dependency snapshot.
sha.human_parameter_description: The commit SHA for the code state you’re capturing. Use the full 40‑character SHA to avoid ambiguity.

repo.title: Repo
repo.description: Repository name, without `.git` extension (name is not case-sensitive).
repo.human_parameter_description: The name of the repository (without .git) that you want to snapshot. This identifies which project’s dependencies to capture.

owner.title: Owner
owner.description: Account owner of the repository (name is not case-sensitive).
owner.human_parameter_description: The user or organization that owns the repository you want to snapshot. This tells us where to find the repo.

job__id.title: Job  Id
job__id.description: Optional external ID of the job that generated this snapshot.
job__id.human_parameter_description: An ID for the CI job or process that produced this snapshot. It helps you trace the snapshot back to the run that created it.

scanned.title: Scanned
scanned.description: UTC timestamp (ISO 8601 format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ) when the snapshot was taken.
scanned.human_parameter_description: The exact time the snapshot was taken, in UTC ISO 8601 format (e.g., 2023-10-26T14:30:00Z). This timestamps when the dependency state was captured.

version.title: Version
version.description: Version of the dependency snapshot submission, typically of the manifest or lock file format.
version.human_parameter_description: The version number of the snapshot format you’re submitting. Use the version that matches your manifest/lockfile format or tool.

metadata.title: Metadata
metadata.description: Optional user-defined metadata as a JSON string for domain-specific information. Limited to 8 keys with scalar values (e.g., string, number, boolean). Example: '{"key1": "value1", "key2": 123}'
metadata.human_parameter_description: Optional key‑value details you want to attach to this snapshot (up to 8 simple values) as a JSON string. Use this for filtering, auditing, or custom notes.

manifests.title: Manifests
manifests.description: Optional collection of package manifests as a JSON string (e.g., package-lock.json, pom.xml). Keys are manifest file names; values detail dependencies. Example: '{"package-lock.json": {"name": "...", "resolved": {...}}}'
manifests.human_parameter_description: A mapping of manifest file names to their dependency details from your scan as a JSON string (e.g., package-lock.json, pom.xml). Include the files you analyzed.

detector__url.title: Detector  Url
detector__url.description: Optional URL of the detector tool used.
detector__url.human_parameter_description: A URL for the dependency scanning tool or its documentation. Helpful for reference.

detector__name.title: Detector  Name
detector__name.description: Optional name of the tool used to detect dependencies.
detector__name.human_parameter_description: The name of the tool that scanned your project for dependencies. Examples include 'dependency-check' or similar tools.

job__html__url.title: Job  Html  Url
job__html__url.description: Optional URL for the job that generated this snapshot.
job__html__url.human_parameter_description: A link to the CI job or build page that created this snapshot. Useful for others to see logs and details.

job__correlator.title: Job  Correlator
job__correlator.description: Optional string to group snapshots. For a given `job.correlator` and `detector.name`, only the 'latest' snapshot is current. Useful to distinguish detection runs (e.g., concatenating GITHUB_WORKFLOW and GITHUB_JOB).
job__correlator.human_parameter_description: A string that groups related snapshots from the same workflow or run. It helps keep only the latest snapshot current for that group.

detector__version.title: Detector  Version
detector__version.description: Optional version of the detector tool used.
detector__version.human_parameter_description: The version of the dependency scanning tool you used. It helps track which tool release produced the results.

message.title: Message
message.description: A message providing further details about the result, such as why the dependencies were not updated.

created_at.title: Created At
created_at.description: The time at which the snapshot was scanned.

items.name: Create a tag object
items.description: Creates an annotated Git tag object in a repository, pointing to an existing Git object (commit, tree, or blob) defined by its SHA and ensuring the `type` field correctly specifies the object's type.

input_parameters.title: CreateATagObjectRequest

tag.title: Tag
tag.description: The name of the tag, typically a version identifier (e.g., "v0.0.1").
tag.human_parameter_description: The label you want to give the tag (for example 'v1.0.0'). This helps others identify the release or snapshot.

repo.title: Repo
repo.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This name is not case-sensitive.
repo.human_parameter_description: The repository name where you'll create the tag. Don't include the .git extension.

type.title: Type
type.description: The type of the Git object being tagged.
type.human_parameter_description: Choose what kind of object the SHA refers to—commit, tree, or blob—so the tag points to the right thing.

owner.title: Owner
owner.description: The account owner of the repository. This name is not case-sensitive.
owner.human_parameter_description: The username or organization that owns the repository where you want to create the tag.

object.title: Object
object.description: The SHA of the Git object (commit, tree, or blob) that this tag is pointing to.
object.human_parameter_description: The exact SHA of the commit, tree, or blob you want this tag to point to. You can copy this from the item you’re tagging.

message.title: Message
message.description: The message associated with the tag.
message.human_parameter_description: A short note explaining what’s in this tag or why you’re creating it, such as release notes.

tagger__date.title: Tagger  Date
tagger__date.description: The timestamp for when this object was tagged. This should be in ISO 8601 format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.
tagger__date.human_parameter_description: The date and time you want to record for this tag. Leave blank to use the current time.

tagger__name.title: Tagger  Name
tagger__name.description: The name of the person creating the tag.
tagger__name.human_parameter_description: The name you want to appear as the author of this tag.

tagger__email.title: Tagger  Email
tagger__email.description: The email address of the person creating the tag.
tagger__email.human_parameter_description: The email address you want to record for the tag’s author (used for attribution).

items.name: Create a tree
items.description: Creates a new Git tree object in a repository, defining file/directory structure by specifying tree entries, optionally building on a `base_tree` SHA; all provided SHAs must be valid.

input_parameters.title: CreateATreeRequest

repo.title: Repo
repo.description: The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.
repo.human_parameter_description: The repository name where the new tree should be created. This tells us which project you’re updating.

tree.title: Tree
tree.description: Array of objects defining the tree structure. Each object (node) requires `path` (string), `mode` (string; e.g., '100644' file, '100755' executable, '040000' subdirectory/tree, '160000' submodule, '120000' symlink), and `type` (string: 'blob', 'tree', or 'commit'). For new/updated blobs, provide `content` (UTF-8 string). For existing objects or `tree`/`commit` types, provide `sha` (string). To delete, specify `path`, `mode`, `type`, and set `sha` to `null`.
tree.human_parameter_description: The list of files and folders you want to add, update, or delete in the repository. Each entry describes a path and what to do with it so GitHub knows what to create or change.

owner.title: Owner
owner.description: The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.
owner.human_parameter_description: The username or organization that owns the repository where you want to create the tree. Provide the account name exactly as it appears on GitHub.

base_tree.title: Base Tree
base_tree.description: SHA1 of an existing Git tree object to use as a base. If provided, its entries are combined with `tree` entries, where `tree` entries overwrite those from `base_tree` with the same path. Typically the SHA1 of the latest commit's tree for new branch changes. If omitted, the new tree is built from `tree` entries; files from the parent commit's tree not in `tree` are treated as deleted.
base_tree.human_parameter_description: An existing tree SHA to start from, so you can build your changes on top of a known state. Use this to modify only what’s different instead of redefining the whole tree.

items.name: Find Pull Requests
items.description: Primary tool to find and search pull requests. Supports filtering by repository, author, state, labels, and merge status, and returns structured PR data for reliable use in workflows. GitHub search results are capped at ~1000 total items; narrow filters when totals approach this limit. `created_since`/`updated_since` filter on creation/update timestamps, not `merged_at`; apply merge-date filtering client-side.

input_parameters.title: FindPullRequestsRequest

page.title: Page
page.description: Page number of results to fetch.
page.human_parameter_description: Which page of results to view. Use this to move through large result sets.

repo.title: Repo
repo.description: Filter by specific repository. Can be provided in 'owner/repo' format (e.g., 'facebook/react'), or as just the repo name when used with the owner parameter. When owner and repo are both provided and have the same value, they are combined as 'owner/repo'. When omitted along with owner, search scope is determined by for_authenticated_user flag. The repository must exist and be accessible with your token. Prefer 'owner/repo' format; bare repo name without the `owner` parameter causes invalid repository format errors.
repo.human_parameter_description: Limit the search to a single repository. You can provide it in 'owner/repo' format like 'facebook/react', or just the repository name (like 'react') when also providing the owner parameter separately. If you want to search repository 'notetake/notetake', you can use repo='notetake/notetake' OR owner='notetake' with repo='notetake'. Leave blank to search across multiple repositories. The repository must exist and be accessible with your token.

sort.title: Sort
sort.description: Field to sort results by. Set explicitly to 'updated' with `order=desc` when recency matters; default behavior may return best-match relevance ordering instead.
sort.human_parameter_description: Choose how to sort the results, such as by last updated, creation date, or number of comments.

label.title: Label
label.description: Filter by label name.
label.human_parameter_description: Only include PRs with a particular label, such as 'bug' or 'enhancement'.

order.title: Order
order.human_parameter_description: Pick ascending or descending order for the selected sort field. Most recent first is 'desc'.

owner.title: Owner
owner.description: Filter by repository owner (user or organization). Can be used alone to search all repositories for an owner, or combined with repo parameter to specify owner and repo separately. When both owner and repo are provided, the search is scoped to 'owner/repo'. When omitted along with repo, search scope is determined by for_authenticated_user flag. The owner must exist and repositories must be accessible with your token.
owner.human_parameter_description: Search within all repositories for a specific user or organization (like 'microsoft'), or provide it together with the repo parameter to specify owner and repository separately. If owner='notetake' and repo='notetake', the search will be in repository 'notetake/notetake'. Leave blank to search across multiple owners. The owner must exist and repositories must be accessible with your token.

query.title: Query
query.description: Optional search query for PR title, description, or commit messages. Supports GitHub search syntax including label filters (e.g., 'label:bug'), logical operators (AND, OR, NOT), and text search. If not provided, PRs will be listed based on other filter parameters. Type qualifiers (type:pr, is:pr, is:issue, type:issue) are automatically normalized. When using logical operators with qualifiers like labels, the query is automatically grouped for proper parsing. When omitting query, ensure at least one structured filter parameter is provided; passing no query and no filters may cause validation errors. Prefer dedicated parameters (`label`, `state`, `author`) over embedding qualifiers in the query string. Exact title matching is not supported; post-filter on title client-side if needed.
query.human_parameter_description: Enter words or phrases that appear in the PR title, description, or commit messages. You can also use GitHub search qualifiers like 'label:bug' or combine them with logical operators like 'label:bug OR label:enhancement'. This is optional - you can filter PRs by repository, state, owner, and other parameters without a text search query. Do not include type qualifiers like 'type:pr' or 'is:pr' as they are handled automatically.

state.title: State
state.description: Filter by PR state: 'open', 'closed', or 'all'.
state.human_parameter_description: Choose which PR states to include: open, closed, or all. Use 'all' to see every state.

author.title: Author
author.description: Filter by PR author username. Must be a valid GitHub username (alphanumeric characters and hyphens only, cannot start or end with hyphen). No dots or other special characters allowed.
author.human_parameter_description: Find PRs created by a particular GitHub user. Enter their exact username (case-insensitive). GitHub usernames can only contain letters, numbers, and hyphens (no dots or other special characters). The user must exist on GitHub.

assignee.title: Assignee
assignee.description: Filter by PR assignee username. Use '@me' for current user. Must be a valid GitHub username (alphanumeric characters and hyphens only, cannot start or end with hyphen). No dots or other special characters allowed.
assignee.human_parameter_description: Find PRs assigned to a specific user. Enter their exact username or use '@me' for yourself. GitHub usernames can only contain letters, numbers, and hyphens (no dots or other special characters). The user must exist on GitHub.

language.title: Language
language.human_parameter_description: Restrict results to PRs in repositories primarily using a specific language, like Python or JavaScript.

mentions.title: Mentions
mentions.description: Filter by username mentioned in PR. Must be a valid GitHub username (alphanumeric characters and hyphens only, cannot start or end with hyphen). No dots or other special characters allowed.
mentions.human_parameter_description: Find PRs where a user is mentioned in the discussion. Enter their exact username or use '@me' for yourself. GitHub usernames can only contain letters, numbers, and hyphens (no dots or other special characters). The user must exist on GitHub.

per_page.title: Per Page
per_page.description: Number of results per page (maximum 100). GitHub caps total search results at ~1000 items; iterate `page` until results fewer than `per_page` are returned, and add `repo`, `label`, or date filters when totals approach 1000.
per_page.human_parameter_description: How many results to show per page. Higher numbers return more results at once (up to 100).

is_merged.title: Is Merged
is_merged.description: Filter by merge status. True for merged PRs, False for unmerged, None for all.
is_merged.human_parameter_description: Filter for PRs that have been merged or not. Leave blank to include both.

base_branch.title: Base Branch
base_branch.human_parameter_description: Show PRs targeting a specific base branch (the branch being merged into), like 'main' or 'develop'.

head_branch.title: Head Branch
head_branch.human_parameter_description: Show PRs coming from a specific feature branch (the branch being merged), like 'feature/login'.

created_since.title: Created Since
created_since.description: Filter PRs created after this date (ISO 8601 format). Provide as UTC ISO 8601 timestamp to avoid off-by-one-day errors at range boundaries. Does not filter on `merged_at`.
created_since.human_parameter_description: Include only PRs opened on or after this date. Use ISO dates like '2024-01-01' or '2024-01-01T00:00:00Z'.

updated_since.title: Updated Since
updated_since.description: Filter PRs updated after this date (ISO 8601 format).
updated_since.human_parameter_description: Include only PRs updated on or after this date. Use ISO dates like '2024-01-01' or '2024-01-01T00:00:00Z'.

response_detail.title: Response Detail
response_detail.description: Level of detail in the response. 'minimal' (default) returns an optimized response for AI agents. 'full' returns the complete GitHub API response.
response_detail.human_parameter_description: Choose 'minimal' for a cleaner, AI-optimized summary, or 'full' for the complete GitHub API response.

for_authenticated_user.title: For Authenticated User
for_authenticated_user.description: Include private repositories accessible to the authenticated user in search results. When True without repo/owner, searches PRs involving you (author, assignee, mentions, commenter) across all accessible repos. When False without repo/owner, restricts to public repos only. When repo/owner is specified, this flag has no effect on scope. Set to True when searching private repositories; False searches all of GitHub and produces large noisy result sets.
for_authenticated_user.human_parameter_description: Turn this on to include private repositories you can access with your GitHub account. When no specific repo/owner is provided, this searches PRs where you're involved (author, assignee, mentioned, or commenter). Leave it off to search only public repositories.

items.name: Find Repositories

Check `incomplete_results` in the response — when true, results are non-exhaustive. Search endpoints are rate-limited to ~30 requests/minute (vs. 5000/hour for general REST); apply backoff on 403/429. Total results are capped at ~1000 per query regardless of pagination.

Multi-word phrases in OR expressions are automatically quoted. GitHub limits OR expressions to 6 terms maximum; queries exceeding this limit are truncated. If using GitHub qualifiers like 'repo:', 'user:', or 'org:', they must be properly formatted (e.g., 'repo:owner/name', 'user:username', 'org:orgname'). Note: 'owner:' is not a valid GitHub qualifier; if used, it will be automatically transformed to 'user:'. Must be non-empty; blank strings trigger a 'Search query cannot be empty' validation error.

You can also use GitHub search qualifiers like 'repo:owner/name' to search in a specific repository, 'user:username' for a specific user's repos, or 'org:orgname' for an organization's repos. items.name: Get a reference
items.description: Retrieves a specific Git reference (e.g., a branch, tag, or fully qualified like 'heads/main') from a GitHub repository. The reference must exist in the repository; use 'list_matching_references' first if unsure what references are available.

input_parameters.title: GetAReferenceRequest

ref.title: Ref
ref.description: The Git reference to retrieve. Must be formatted as `heads/<branch_name>` for branches, `tags/<tag_name>` for tags, or `pull/<number>/head` (or `pull/<number>/merge`) for pull requests. Simple branch names (e.g., `main`) are automatically converted to `heads/<name>`. The reference must exist in the repository; a 404 error is returned if not found. If unsure which references exist, use 'list_matching_references' or 'get_a_branch' first. Note: Commit SHAs are not supported by this endpoint; use commit-specific endpoints instead. Not all repositories use 'master'; many now use 'main' as the default branch.
ref.human_parameter_description: The branch, tag, or pull request reference to retrieve. Format as 'heads/branch_name' for branches, 'tags/tag_name' for tags, or 'pull/number/head' for PRs. Simple names like 'main' are treated as branches and converted to 'heads/main'. The reference must exist (404 if not found). If unsure, list references first with 'list_matching_references'. Note: Commit SHAs are not supported by this endpoint.

repo.title: Repo
repo.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This field is not case-sensitive.
repo.human_parameter_description: The name of the repository you want to get the reference from (without .git). This tells us which project under the owner to use.

owner.title: Owner
owner.description: The username or organization name that owns the repository. This field is not case-sensitive.
owner.human_parameter_description: The GitHub account or organization that owns the repository you want to access. Enter the username (like 'octocat') or org name (like 'google') so we can find the right repo.

GetInteractionRestrictionsForAnOrganizat.description:
Response schema for `GetInteractionRestrictionsForAnOrganization`.

When interaction restrictions are active, the response contains:
- `limit`: The type of GitHub user allowed to interact. One of: `existing_users`, `contributors_only`, `collaborators_only`
- `origin`: The source of the restriction (e.g., "organization")
- `expires_at`: ISO 8601 timestamp when the restriction expires

Example (when restrictions are active):
```json
{
  "limit": "collaborators_only",
  "origin": "organization",
  "expires_at": "2018-08-17T04:18:39Z"
}
```

When no restrictions are set, the response is an empty object `{}`.

items.description: Retrieves a file's Base64 encoded content or lists a directory's contents from a GitHub repository.

input_parameters.title: GetRepositoryContentRequest

ref.title: Ref
ref.description: The name of the commit, branch, or tag to read from. Use this parameter to specify which branch (e.g., 'feat/godlocal-dev', 'main', 'develop'), tag (e.g., 'v1.2.0'), or commit SHA you want to access. If not provided, the repository's default branch will be used. Note: Branch names should be passed here, NOT in the path parameter.
ref.human_parameter_description: The branch, tag, or commit to read from. Use this to specify branches like 'feat/godlocal-dev', 'main', or 'develop'. Leave empty to use the repository's default branch (often 'main'). IMPORTANT: Pass branch names here, not in the path parameter.

path.title: Path
path.description: Required. Path to file or directory in the repository. Empty string ('') retrieves root directory contents. Leading slashes auto-stripped. CRITICAL: Do NOT pass branch names here (e.g., 'feat/godlocal-dev', 'main'). Branch names belong in the `ref` parameter. Path should be file/directory path only (e.g., 'src/main.js', 'README.md'), NOT prefixed with branch name (use 'src/main.js' not 'main/src/main.js'). File paths must include extension (e.g., 'README.md', not 'README'). For common files (README, LICENSE, CHANGELOG) without extensions, action auto-tries common extensions (.md, .txt, .rst). Paths are case-sensitive. On 404 errors, list parent directory to verify exact path/casing.
path.human_parameter_description: The file or folder path inside the repository that you want to retrieve. Examples include 'README.md', 'src/main.js', or a directory like 'docs'. Use an empty string to list the root directory contents. Leading slashes are automatically removed. CRITICAL: Do NOT pass branch names here (like 'feat/something', 'main', 'develop'). To specify a branch, tag, or commit, use the `ref` parameter instead. The path should only contain the file/directory path within the repository. Do NOT include the branch name as a prefix - use 'README.md' not 'main/README.md'. Important: Include file extensions (e.g., 'README.md' not just 'README'). For common files like README, LICENSE, or CHANGELOG, the action will try common extensions automatically if not specified. Note: Paths are case-sensitive - 'Docker' and 'docker' are treated as different paths. If you get a 'Not Found' error, try listing the parent directory first to verify the exact path and casing.

repo.title: Repo
repo.description: Required. The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This name is not case sensitive.
repo.human_parameter_description: The repository within that account that you want to read from. Provide its short name without .git, like 'Spoon-Knife'.

owner.title: Owner

owner.human_parameter_description: The username or organization that owns the repository you want to access. This tells us which account to look in. You can also provide the full repository path like 'owner/repo' and it will be parsed automatically.

items.description: Lists issue comments, including those on pull requests, for an accessible repository.

page.title: Page
page.description: The page number of the results to fetch, used for pagination. Default is 1. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."
page.human_parameter_description: The page number of results to view. Use this to move forward or backward through paginated results.

repo.title: Repo
repo.description: REQUIRED. The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This is a path parameter needed to construct the API URL. This field is not case-sensitive.
repo.human_parameter_description: REQUIRED. The name of the repository you want to get issue comments from. This identifies which project to search. This field must be provided.

sort.title: SortEnm
sort.description: Specifies the field by which to sort the issue comments. Valid values are `created` (for creation date, default) or `updated` (for last update date).
sort.human_parameter_description: How you want the comments ordered: by when they were created or when they were last updated. Choose the option that matches how you prefer to review them.

owner.title: Owner
owner.description: REQUIRED. The username of the account or the organization name that owns the repository. This is a path parameter needed to construct the API URL. This field is not case-sensitive.
owner.human_parameter_description: REQUIRED. The account or organization that owns the repository whose issue comments you want to list. Enter the GitHub username or organization name. This field must be provided.

since.title: Since
since.description: Filters comments to include only those last updated at or after the specified time. This should be a timestamp in ISO 8601 format (e.g., `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`).
since.human_parameter_description: Only include comments updated on or after this date and time to filter out older activity. Use an ISO 8601 timestamp, for example 2023-01-01T10:00:00Z.

per_page.title: Per Page
per_page.description: The number of issue comments to retrieve per page. Default is 30, maximum is 100. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."
per_page.human_parameter_description: How many comments to show per page of results. Higher numbers show more at once; lower numbers make pages shorter and faster to scan.

direction.title: DirectionEnm
direction.description: The direction for sorting results. Valid values are `asc` (ascending) or `desc` (descending). This parameter is effective only when `sort` is also specified.
direction.human_parameter_description: Whether to sort in ascending or descending order. Pick this to see newest or oldest comments first.

items.name: List notifications for authenticated user
items.description: Tool to list notification threads for the authenticated user with efficient polling support. Use when you need to fetch the user's GitHub notification inbox with filters like unread/participating/since. Returns notification threads plus polling headers (Last-Modified, ETag, X-Poll-Interval) for efficient polling. IMPORTANT: This endpoint requires a Personal Access Token (classic) with 'notifications' or 'repo' scope. It does NOT work with GitHub App tokens or fine-grained personal access tokens. items.name: List workflow runs for a repository
items.description: Lists workflow runs for a repository, allowing filtering by actor, branch, event, status, creation date, check suite ID, or head SHA; the repository must exist and be accessible.

input_parameters.title: ListWorkflowRunsForARepositoryRequest

page.title: Page
page.description: Page number of the results to fetch.
page.human_parameter_description: Which page of results to view. Combine with Results per page to navigate through all runs.

repo.title: Repo
repo.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension (not case-sensitive).
repo.human_parameter_description: The name of the repository where you want to list workflow runs. Enter it exactly as it appears on GitHub (without .git).

actor.title: Actor
actor.description: Filter by the actor's login (e.g., the user who triggered the `push`).
actor.human_parameter_description: Enter the GitHub username of the person who triggered the runs you’re looking for. This narrows results to runs started by that user.

event.title: Event
event.description: Filter by the event that triggered the workflow (e.g., `push`, `pull_request`).
event.human_parameter_description: Choose the type of event that triggered the runs, such as push or pull_request. This helps you focus on runs started by a specific kind of activity.

owner.title: Owner
owner.description: The account owner of the repository (not case-sensitive).
owner.human_parameter_description: The GitHub username or organization that owns the repository you want to view. Use the account name exactly as it appears on GitHub.

branch.title: Branch
branch.description: Filter by branch name (e.g., `main` or the branch that triggered the `push`).
branch.human_parameter_description: Filter runs to a specific branch, like main or develop. Leave blank to include runs from all branches.

status.title: StatusEnm
status.description: Filter by `status` or `conclusion` (e.g., `success`, `in_progress`). Note: Only GitHub Actions can set `waiting`, `pending`, or `requested`.
status.human_parameter_description: Select the current state or outcome of the runs you want to see, like success, in_progress, or queued. Use this to find runs that finished a certain way or are still running.

created.title: Created
created.description: Filter by creation date or date-time range (ISO8601 format: YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ). Supports operators like `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=`, and `..` for ranges.
created.human_parameter_description: Filter runs by when they were created. You can provide a single date or a date range in ISO format to narrow the timeframe.

head_sha.title: Head Sha
head_sha.description: Filter to include only runs associated with the specified `head_sha` (commit SHA at the head of the branch).
head_sha.human_parameter_description: Filter runs associated with a specific commit. Paste the full commit SHA to see runs for that exact revision.

per_page.title: Per Page
per_page.description: Number of results per page (maximum 100).
per_page.human_parameter_description: How many results to show on each page. Use a higher number to see more runs at once (up to 100).

check_suite_id.title: Check Suite Id
check_suite_id.human_parameter_description: Show only runs that belong to a specific check suite. Use this if you have a check suite ID from another view or previous step.

exclude_pull_requests.title: Exclude Pull Requests
exclude_pull_requests.description: Set to `true` to exclude workflow runs triggered by pull request events. Omit or leave as null to include all runs.
exclude_pull_requests.human_parameter_description: Turn this on to hide runs triggered by pull requests, showing only runs from other events like pushes. Leave it off to include pull request runs.

A 405 error can occur for multiple reasons: (1) The PR is still in draft mode - convert it to ready-for-review first using GITHUB_UPDATE_A_PULL_REQUEST. items.human_description:
This action merges an open pull request in a repository. You can specify details like the merge method and commit message.

**IMPORTANT: A 405 error can occur for multiple reasons:**
- **Draft PRs cannot be merged.** If the pull request is still in draft mode, you must first mark it as ready for review before merging. Use the GITHUB_UPDATE_A_PULL_REQUEST action or the GitHub web UI to convert the draft to a regular PR.
- **Branch protection rules not satisfied.** The repository may have branch protection rules requiring approving reviews, passing status checks, or other conditions. Check the error message for details like "At least 1 approving review is required" or "Required status checks have not passed".
- **Base branch was modified.** If the base branch has been updated since the PR was last synced, you must update the PR branch first. Use the GITHUB_UPDATE_A_PULL_REQUEST_BRANCH action to sync the PR with the latest base branch changes, then retry the merge.

This endpoint returns an empty response body on success with HTTP status code 204 (No Content).
The successful removal of a repository from an app installation does not return any data fields.

Status codes:
- 204: No Content - Repository successfully removed from app installation. Response body is empty.
- 304: Not modified - Resource has not been modified since last request.
- 403: Forbidden - User lacks required admin access to the repository or the endpoint is being accessed with an unsupported token type.
- 404: Resource not found - The specified installation or repository does not exist, or the user does not have access.
- 422: Unprocessable Entity - Returned when the application is installed on all repositories in the organization, or if this request would remove the last repository that the application has access to in the organization.

Notes:
- This endpoint only works for PATs (classic) with the repo scope
- Does not work with GitHub App user access tokens, GitHub App installation access tokens, or fine-grained personal access tokens
- The authenticated user must have admin access to the repository
- The installation must have repository_selection of 'selected'

items.name: Replace repository access for an org Codespaces secret
items.description: Replaces the list of repositories that can access an organization-level Codespaces secret. This operation completely replaces the existing list of repositories with the provided list. The secret must already have its visibility set to 'selected' for this operation to succeed. Use this when you want to set an exact list of repositories that should have access. Prerequisites: - The organization must exist and you must have admin:org scope - The Codespaces secret must already exist in the organization - The secret's visibility must be set to 'selected' (not 'all' or 'private') Returns HTTP 204 No Content on success, 404 if secret/org not found, 409 if visibility is not 'selected'.

items.name: Run GraphQL Query
items.description: Tool to run an arbitrary GitHub GraphQL v4 query or mutation. Use when fetching multiple datasets in one batch. Cost-based rate limit: ~5,000 points/hour; keep field selections narrow, avoid deep nesting, and include rateLimit in responses to monitor quota. Responses are nested under data.data (e.g., data.data.repository.vulnerabilityAlerts); always inspect the errors array even on HTTP 200, as partial failures embed there. Paginate by looping on pageInfo.hasNextPage and advancing with pageInfo.endCursor. Search results cap at ~1,000 items per query; split by label, date range, or repository for full coverage. Use ProjectV2 nodes, not Classic Projects (deprecated). Parallel mutations (e.g., addProjectV2ItemById) can trigger transient conflicts; use sequential execution.

For reliable searches, avoid boolean operators and parentheses. Supports qualifiers: `language:`, `repo:`, `path:`, `extension:`, `user:`, `org:`, `in:file`. Multiple terms use implicit AND: `hello world` finds both. Quote exact phrases: `"exact phrase"`. For complex boolean logic, use multiple separate API calls or the GitHub web interface.

items.name: Search commits
items.description: Finds commits on GitHub using a query string (q) supporting keywords and qualifiers, with options for sorting and pagination.

input_parameters.title: SearchCommitsRequest

q.title: Q
q.description: Search query with at least one text keyword plus optional qualifiers. GitHub requires actual search text (commit message keywords) - qualifiers alone are not allowed. Common qualifiers: 'repo:owner/name', 'author:username', 'committer:username', 'author-date:YYYY-MM-DD' or 'author-date:>YYYY-MM-DD..YYYY-MM-DD', 'committer-date:YYYY-MM-DD', 'merge:true/false', 'hash:HASH', 'parent:HASH', 'tree:HASH'. IMPORTANT: The 'hash:' qualifier requires a full 40-character hexadecimal commit hash (e.g., 'hash:e5bd3914e2e596debea16f433f57875b5b90bcd6'). Do NOT use branch names, tag names, or short refs with 'hash:' - use 'repo:owner/name' with other filters to search commits on a specific branch.
q.human_parameter_description: Enter search text keywords (words to find in commit messages) plus optional filters like repo, author, or date. You must include at least some search text - you cannot use filters alone.

page.title: Page
page.description: Page number of results to retrieve.
page.human_parameter_description: Which page of results you want to see. Use 1 for the first page.

sort.title: SortEnm
sort.description: Sorts results by 'author-date' or 'committer-date'. Use separately with the 'order' parameter (e.g., sort='committer-date' with order='desc'). Do not combine them into a single value. If unspecified, GitHub defaults to 'best match' ranking.
sort.human_parameter_description: Choose how to sort the results: by the author's commit date or the committer's date. Use this with the order parameter to control sort direction. Leave this blank to use best-match ranking.

order.title: Order
order.description: Sort order: 'desc' (newest first) or 'asc' (oldest first). Use with the 'sort' parameter to control direction (e.g., sort='committer-date' with order='desc').
order.human_parameter_description: Pick whether sorted results should show newest to oldest (desc) or oldest to newest (asc). This works together with the sort parameter.

per_page.title: Per Page

items.name: Search issues and pull requests
items.description: Searches GitHub for issues and pull requests. Supports keywords, qualifiers (repo:, org:, user:, state:, label:, author:, assignee:, mentions:, etc.), and type filters (is:issue, is:pr). Type filters cannot be used alone - they must be combined with at least one keyword or other qualifier. All other qualifiers work independently. The @me shorthand (e.g., assignee:@me, mentions:@me) is automatically resolved to your username. Logical operators (AND, OR, NOT) are supported but limited to a maximum of 5 operators total per query.

input_parameters.title: SearchIssuesAndPullRequestsRequest

q.title: Q
examples: bug repo:octocat/Spoon-Knife is:issue is:open label:"help wanted"
q.description: Search query using GitHub's search syntax. Supports keywords, qualifiers (repo:, org:, user:, state:, label:, author:, assignee:, mentions:, etc.), and type filters (is:issue, is:pr). IMPORTANT: Type filters (is:issue, is:pr) cannot be used alone - they must be combined with at least one keyword or other qualifier. All other qualifiers work independently (e.g., 'state:open', 'label:bug', 'assignee:octocat'). The @me shorthand (e.g., assignee:@me, mentions:@me, author:@me) can be used to reference the authenticated user. Logical operators (AND, OR, NOT) can be used to combine terms (maximum 5 operators total).

Must use real GitHub usernames/orgs (e.g., `user:octocat`), not placeholders. Queries with logical operators must include at least one plain keyword; `topic:solana OR topic:ethereum` fails, use `solana OR ethereum stars:>100` instead.

IMPORTANT: Use at most 5 AND/OR/NOT operators in your query.

sort.human_parameter_description: Choose how the results should be sorted, such as by stars, forks, help-wanted issues, most recently updated, or creation date. Leave this blank to use GitHub's best match.

items.name: Unlock an organization repository
items.description: Unlocks a repository that was locked for migration within a GitHub organization. This action is part of the organization migrations workflow. When you start a migration with `lock_repositories=true`, the source repositories are locked to prevent changes during export. After the migration is complete and applied to the target instance, use this action to unlock the repositories so they can be accessed or deleted. Requirements: - You must be an organization owner to unlock repositories - The repository must be currently locked as part of the specified migration - This endpoint does not work with GitHub App tokens or fine-grained personal access tokens Typical workflow: 1. Start an organization migration with POST /orgs/{org}/migrations 2. Wait for the migration to complete (state: "exported") 3. Apply the migration to your target instance 4. Unlock each migrated repository using this action 5. Delete the source repositories if no longer needed

items.name: Update a reference
items.description: Updates an existing Git reference (e.g., a branch or tag) to point to a specific commit SHA. By default, only allows fast-forward updates (where the new commit is a descendant of the current one). Set `force=true` to allow non-fast-forward updates that rewrite history. IMPORTANT: The reference must already exist - use 'Create a reference' action to create new refs.

input_parameters.title: UpdateAReferenceRequest

ref.title: Ref
ref.description: The name of the Git reference to update WITHOUT the 'refs/' prefix. For branches: use 'heads/<branch-name>' (e.g., 'heads/main', 'heads/feature-branch'). For tags: use 'tags/<tag-name>' (e.g., 'tags/v1.0.0'). Note: Branch references require 'heads/' (plural), not 'head/' (singular). Bare branch names will be automatically prefixed with 'heads/'. The reference must already exist - this endpoint only updates existing refs.
ref.human_parameter_description: The branch or tag path you want to update (without 'refs/' prefix). Use 'heads/branch-name' for branches or 'tags/tag-name' for tags. The reference must already exist.

sha.title: Sha
sha.description: The SHA1 commit hash to point this reference to. Must be exactly 40 hexadecimal characters (0-9, a-f) representing a valid commit that exists in the repository.
sha.human_parameter_description: The full 40-character commit hash you want the reference to point to. Find this by viewing commits in your repository - it's the long hexadecimal string identifying each commit.

repo.title: Repo
repo.description: Repository name, excluding `.git` extension (case-insensitive).
repo.human_parameter_description: The name of the repository where you want to update the reference. Use the exact name from the GitHub URL (without .git).

force.title: Force
force.description: Controls whether to allow non-fast-forward updates. When `false` (default), the new commit must be a direct descendant of the current commit (fast-forward only) - this prevents accidental history rewriting. When `true`, allows moving the reference to any commit, even if it means rewriting history or moving backward. Set to `true` only when you need to force-push changes, reset a branch, or intentionally rewrite commit history.
force.human_parameter_description: Set to true only if you need to rewrite history or move the branch backward. Leave false (default) for normal forward updates where the new commit builds upon the current one.

owner.title: Owner
owner.description: Account owner of the repository (case-insensitive).
owner.human_parameter_description: The GitHub username or organization that owns the repository you want to change. Use the owner shown in the repository URL.

items.name: Update a release
items.description: Updates an existing release in a GitHub repository, allowing modification of its attributes; if linking a discussion, the `discussion_category_name` must refer to an existing category in the repository.

input_parameters.title: UpdateAReleaseRequest

body.title: Body
examples: This release includes performance improvements and bug fixes related to user authentication.
body.description: Text describing the contents of the release. Supports GitHub Flavored Markdown.
body.human_parameter_description: The release notes describing what's new, fixed, or changed. You can format this with Markdown for readability.

name.title: Name
name.human_parameter_description: A clear title for the release that people will see on the releases page (for example, Version 1.0.1).

repo.title: Repo
repo.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This name is not case-sensitive.
repo.human_parameter_description: The name of the repository where the release lives. Use the short repo name (for example, Hello-World).

draft.title: Draft
draft.description: Set to `true` to mark the release as a draft, or `false` to publish it. Default: `false`.
draft.human_parameter_description: Save the release as a draft so you can review it privately before publishing. Set to false to make it public.

owner.title: Owner
owner.description: The account owner of the repository. This name is not case-sensitive.
owner.human_parameter_description: The username or organization that owns the repository you want to update. This helps us find the right repo.

tag_name.title: Tag Name
tag_name.description: The name of the tag. This can be an existing tag or a new tag name.
tag_name.human_parameter_description: The tag you want this release to use (for example, v1.0.1). Use an existing tag or enter a new one to version the release.

prerelease.title: Prerelease
prerelease.description: Set to `true` to identify the release as a pre-release, or `false` for a full release. Default: `false`.
prerelease.human_parameter_description: Mark the release as a pre-release if it’s meant for testing or early access. Leave false for a stable, public release.

release_id.title: Release Id
release_id.description: The unique identifier of the release to be updated.
release_id.human_parameter_description: The unique ID of the release you want to update. You can get it from the release page or a previous list/search.

make_latest.title: Make Latest
make_latest.description: Specifies whether this release should be set as the latest release for the repository. Accepts 'true', 'false', or 'legacy'. Drafts and pre-releases cannot be set as latest. Defaults to `true` for newly published releases. `legacy` specifies that the latest release should be determined based on the release creation date and higher semantic version.
make_latest.human_parameter_description: Choose whether this should be shown as the latest release. Use true to promote it, false to keep the current latest, or 'legacy' to let GitHub decide by version/date.

target_commitish.title: Target Commitish
target_commitish.description: Specifies the commitish value (e.g., branch name or commit SHA) that determines where the Git tag is created from. Can be any branch or commit SHA. This parameter is unused if the Git tag specified by `tag_name` already exists. Defaults to the repository's default branch if omitted.
target_commitish.human_parameter_description: The branch name or commit SHA where the tag should point. Provide this if you're creating or moving the tag; otherwise you can leave it blank.

discussion_category_name.title: Discussion Category Name
discussion_category_name.description: If specified, a discussion of this category is created and linked to the release. The category must already exist in the repository. This parameter is ignored if a discussion is already linked to the release. For more information, see "[Managing categories for discussions in your repository](https://docs.github.com/discussions/managing-discussions-for-your-community/managing-categories-for-discussions-in-your-repository)."
discussion_category_name.human_parameter_description: If you want to start a linked discussion for this release, enter the name of an existing discussion category (for example, Announcements). Leave blank to skip.
