items.name: Update a repository
items.description: Updates settings for an existing GitHub repository, such as name, description, visibility, merge strategies, and security configurations.

input_parameters.title: UpdateARepositoryRequest

name.title: Name
name.description: New name for the repository (not case-sensitive).
name.human_parameter_description: If you want to rename the repository, enter the new name. Leave empty to keep the current name.

repo.title: Repo
repo.description: ACTUAL name of an existing repository, without the `.git` extension (not case-sensitive). MUST be a real repository that exists and is accessible - placeholder values like 'your-repo-name' will cause 404 errors.
repo.human_parameter_description: The ACTUAL name of an existing repository you want to update. This must be a real repository name that exists on GitHub and you have access to, NOT a placeholder like 'your-repo-name' or 'my-repo'. Use the exact name as it appears on GitHub (without .git extension).

owner.title: Owner
owner.description: ACTUAL GitHub username or organization name that owns the repository (not case-sensitive). MUST be a real, existing account - placeholder values like 'your-username' will cause 404 errors.
owner.human_parameter_description: The ACTUAL GitHub account (user or organization) that owns the repository you want to update. This must be a real username/org name that exists on GitHub, NOT a placeholder like 'your-username'.

private.title: Private
private.description: Whether the repository is private. IMPORTANT: Public forks cannot be made private - this is a GitHub platform restriction. Changing visibility may also be restricted by organization policies.
private.human_parameter_description: Choose whether to make the repository private. IMPORTANT: Public forks cannot be made private. Private repositories are only visible to people you grant access to.

archived.title: Archived
archived.description: Archives the repository (making it read-only) or unarchives it.
archived.human_parameter_description: Archive the repository to make it read-only. Turn this off to unarchive.

has_wiki.title: Has Wiki
has_wiki.human_parameter_description: Enable the Wiki to host documentation inside the repository.

homepage.title: Homepage
homepage.human_parameter_description: A website or documentation link you want to display on the repository page.

has_issues.title: Has Issues
has_issues.description: Enables GitHub Issues for this repository.
has_issues.human_parameter_description: Turn on the Issues tab to track bugs and tasks. Disable this if you manage issues elsewhere.

visibility.title: VisibilityEnm
visibility.description: Repository visibility. IMPORTANT: Public forks cannot be made private - this is a GitHub platform restriction.
visibility.human_parameter_description: Set how visible the repository should be. IMPORTANT: Public forks cannot be made private. Pick public to share with everyone or private to restrict access.

description.title: Description
examples: A library for advanced data processing.
description.human_parameter_description: A short summary that appears on the repository page. Use this to explain what the project does.

is_template.title: Is Template
is_template.description: Designates this repository as a template repository.
is_template.human_parameter_description: Mark this repository as a template so others can generate new repositories from it.

has_projects.title: Has Projects
has_projects.description: Enables GitHub Projects. Note: Organization settings might override this and cause an error if projects are disabled organization-wide.
has_projects.human_parameter_description: Enable the Projects feature for planning and tracking work. Turn this off if your team uses another tool.

allow_forking.title: Allow Forking
allow_forking.description: Allows private forks of this repository. IMPORTANT: This setting can ONLY be changed for organization-owned repositories. Attempting to set this for user-owned repositories will result in a 422 error. Omit this field if you don't want to change the forking setting.
allow_forking.human_parameter_description: Allow forks of this repository (organization-owned repos only). Leave unset for user-owned repos to avoid errors.

default_branch.title: Default Branch
default_branch.human_parameter_description: Choose which branch should be the default on GitHub. This is shown first and used for new pull requests.

allow_auto_merge.title: Allow Auto Merge
allow_auto_merge.human_parameter_description: Allow eligible pull requests to merge automatically once required checks pass.

allow_merge_commit.title: Allow Merge Commit
allow_merge_commit.description: Allows merging pull requests via merge commits.
allow_merge_commit.human_parameter_description: Allow pull requests to be merged with a merge commit that preserves the full history.

allow_rebase_merge.title: Allow Rebase Merge
allow_rebase_merge.human_parameter_description: Allow pull requests to be merged using rebase to create a linear history.

allow_squash_merge.title: Allow Squash Merge
allow_squash_merge.human_parameter_description: Allow pull requests to be merged using the squash strategy.

merge_commit_title.title: MergeCommitTitleEnm
merge_commit_title.description: Default title for merge commits: 'PR_TITLE' or 'MERGE_MESSAGE'. CONSTRAINT: If set to 'PR_TITLE', merge_commit_message must be 'PR_BODY' or 'BLANK'. If set to 'MERGE_MESSAGE', merge_commit_message must be blank/unset.
merge_commit_title.human_parameter_description: Choose the default title for merge commits. Note: PR_TITLE requires merge_commit_message to be PR_BODY or BLANK.

allow_update_branch.title: Allow Update Branch
allow_update_branch.description: Allows updating a pull request's head branch from the base branch if not strictly required for merging.
allow_update_branch.human_parameter_description: Let maintainers update a pull request’s branch from the base branch even when it isn’t required to merge.

merge_commit_message.title: MergeCommitMessageEnm
merge_commit_message.description: Default message for merge commits: 'PR_BODY', 'PR_TITLE', or 'BLANK'. CONSTRAINT: If merge_commit_title is 'PR_TITLE', this must be 'PR_BODY' or 'BLANK'. Cannot be set when merge_commit_title is 'MERGE_MESSAGE'.
merge_commit_message.human_parameter_description: Choose the default message for merge commits. Must be PR_BODY or BLANK when merge_commit_title is PR_TITLE.

delete_branch_on_merge.title: Delete Branch On Merge
delete_branch_on_merge.description: Automatically deletes head branches after merging pull requests.
delete_branch_on_merge.human_parameter_description: Automatically remove the pull request’s source branch after the merge to keep things tidy.

squash_merge_commit_title.title: SquashMergeCommitTitleEnm
squash_merge_commit_title.description: Default title for squash merge commits: 'PR_TITLE' or 'COMMIT_OR_PR_TITLE'.
squash_merge_commit_title.human_parameter_description: Choose the default title when squash-merging a pull request. Use the PR title or fall back to the commit/PR title.

squash_merge_commit_message.title: SquashMergeCommitMessageEnm
squash_merge_commit_message.description: Default message for squash merge commits: 'PR_BODY', 'COMMIT_MESSAGES', or 'BLANK'.
squash_merge_commit_message.human_parameter_description: Choose what becomes the commit message when squash-merging: the PR body, combined commit messages, or leave it blank.

items.name: Update a repository ruleset
items.description: Updates an existing repository ruleset, identified by `ruleset_id` for a given repository, allowing partial updates to its configuration such as name, target, enforcement, bypass actors, conditions, and rules.

input_parameters.title: UpdateARepositoryRulesetRequest

name.title: Name
name.description: The new name for the ruleset.
name.human_parameter_description: The new name you want to give this ruleset. Leave this blank if you don’t want to change the current name.

repo.title: Repo
repo.description: The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. This name is not case sensitive.
repo.human_parameter_description: The repository you want to update, without the .git extension. Use the name exactly as it appears on GitHub.

owner.title: Owner
owner.description: The account owner of the repository. This name is not case sensitive.
owner.human_parameter_description: The account that owns the repository you want to update. Use the username or organization name as shown on GitHub.

rules.title: Rules
rules.description: String representing rules to enforce. Each rule has a `type` and optional `parameters` (e.g., `[{'type': 'creation'}, {'type': 'pull_request', 'parameters': {'required_approving_review_count': 2}}]`). Accepts both JSON format with double quotes or Python list syntax with single quotes. Refer to GitHub API documentation for available rule types and their parameters.
rules.human_parameter_description: The specific rules you want this ruleset to apply, such as requiring reviews or blocking force pushes. Provide each rule with any needed settings.

target.title: TargetEnm
target.description: The target of the ruleset (e.g., branch or tag).
target.human_parameter_description: Choose whether the rules apply to branches or tags. Pick the option that matches where you want these rules enforced.

ruleset_id.title: Ruleset Id
ruleset_id.description: The unique identifier of the existing ruleset to be updated.
ruleset_id.human_parameter_description: The unique ID of the ruleset you want to update. You can find this in the repository’s ruleset settings or from a previous API response.

enforcement.title: EnforcementEnm
enforcement.description: Specifies the enforcement level: `disabled` (ruleset is ignored), `active` (ruleset is enforced), or `evaluate` (allows testing rules before enforcement - GitHub Enterprise only).
enforcement.human_parameter_description: How strictly to apply this ruleset—disabled, active, or evaluate. Choose 'evaluate' to test the rules without blocking changes.

bypass_actors.title: Bypass Actors
bypass_actors.description: String representing actors that can bypass ruleset. Each actor specifies `actor_id`, `actor_type` (`RepositoryRole`, `Team`, `Integration`, `OrganizationAdmin`), and `bypass_mode` (`always`, `pull_request`). Accepts both JSON format with double quotes or Python list syntax with single quotes. Example: `[{'actor_id': 1, 'actor_type': 'RepositoryRole', 'bypass_mode': 'always'}]`.
bypass_actors.human_parameter_description: Specify who can bypass this ruleset and when. Add teams, roles, apps, or admins that should be allowed to proceed even if the rules would block them.

conditions__ref__name__exclude.title: Conditions  Ref  Name  Exclude
conditions__ref__name__exclude.description: Ref names or patterns (fnmatch-style globs) to exclude. The ruleset will not apply if any of these patterns match.
conditions__ref__name__exclude.human_parameter_description: Branches or tags (or patterns) where this ruleset should not apply. Use this to make exceptions to your include list.

conditions__ref__name__include.title: Conditions  Ref  Name  Include
conditions__ref__name__include.description: Ref names or patterns (fnmatch-style globs) to include for the ruleset to apply. `~DEFAULT_BRANCH` targets the default branch; `~ALL` targets all branches.
conditions__ref__name__include.human_parameter_description: Branches or tags (or patterns) where this ruleset should apply. You can use exact names or wildcards like feature/*.

items.description: Updates a team's settings (e.g., name, description, privacy, parent team) within a GitHub organization, identified by its slug and organization name.

input_parameters.title: UpdateATeamRequest

org.title: Org
org.description: The organization's name (case-insensitive). This is a required path parameter.
org.human_parameter_description: The GitHub organization that contains the team you want to update. Use the organization's short name (as it appears in the URL). This is required.

name.title: Name
name.description: New display name for the team.
name.human_parameter_description: The new display name for the team. Leave empty to keep the current name.

privacy.title: PrivacyEnm
privacy.description:
The desired privacy level for the team. Editing teams without specifying this parameter leaves `privacy` intact. When a team is nested, the `privacy` for parent teams cannot be `secret`.
  - For a non-nested team:
    - `secret`: Visible only to organization owners and members of this team.
    - `closed`: Visible to all members of this organization.
    - `public`: Visible to all members of this organization (equivalent to `closed`).
  - For a parent or child team:
    - `closed`: Visible to all members of this organization.
    - `public`: Visible to all members of this organization (equivalent to `closed`).
privacy.human_parameter_description: Decides who can see this team within your organization. Choose 'secret' to hide it from non-members, 'closed' or 'public' to make it visible to all org members.

team_slug.title: Team Slug
team_slug.description: The team's unique slug identifier (typically URL-friendly version of team name). This is a required path parameter.
team_slug.human_parameter_description: The URL-friendly identifier of the team you want to update. You can copy this from the team's page URL in GitHub. This is required.

permission.title: PermissionEnm
permission.description: **Deprecated**. Default permission (pull, push, or admin) for new repositories added to this team. This may be removed in future versions.
permission.human_parameter_description: The default access level this team gets when you add new repositories to it. Only affects repos added after this change; existing repo permissions stay the same.

description.title: Description
examples: Responsible for all frontend development aspects of Project X
description.description: New team description; an empty string clears the existing description.
description.human_parameter_description: A brief description of what the team does. Leave empty to clear the description, or skip to keep it as is.

parent_team_id.title: Parent Team Id
parent_team_id.description: The unique identifier (ID) of an existing team to set as this team's parent. This establishes a nested team structure. To remove an existing parent team relationship and make this a top-level team, explicitly pass `null` for this field (e.g., by setting this parameter to Python `None`). If this parameter is not provided in the request, the current parent team, if any, remains unchanged.
parent_team_id.human_parameter_description: If you want this team nested under another, enter that parent team’s ID. Leave blank to keep the current parent, or clear it to make this a top-level team.

notification_setting.title: NotificationSettingEnm
notification_setting.description:
The notification setting the team has chosen. Editing teams without specifying this parameter leaves `notification_setting` intact.
  - `notifications_enabled`: Team members receive notifications when the team is @mentioned.
  - `notifications_disabled`: No one receives notifications for team @mentions.
notification_setting.human_parameter_description: Controls whether team members get notifications when the team is mentioned. Turn this on to alert members on @mentions, or off to keep mentions quiet.

items.name: Update branch protection
items.description: Updates the protection settings for an existing branch in a repository, which must not contain wildcard characters.

input_parameters.title: UpdateBranchProtectionRequest

repo.title: Repo
repo.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension (not case-sensitive).
repo.human_parameter_description: The repository name you want to update, without the .git ending. This is the repo where the branch lives.

owner.title: Owner
owner.description: The account owner of the repository (not case-sensitive).
owner.human_parameter_description: The GitHub username or organization that owns the repository you want to update. Use the account name exactly as it appears on GitHub.

branch.title: Branch
branch.description: Name of the branch to protect; wildcard characters are not allowed (use GraphQL API for wildcard support).
branch.human_parameter_description: The exact name of the branch you want to protect, like 'main' or 'develop'. This tells us which branch’s rules to change.

lock_branch.title: Lock Branch
lock_branch.description: If `True`, sets the branch to read-only, preventing pushes.
lock_branch.human_parameter_description: Make the branch read-only so no one can push to it. Useful for freezing a branch.

enforce_admins.title: Enforce Admins
enforce_admins.description: Enforces configured restrictions for repository administrators. Set to `True` to enforce for admins, or `None`/`null` to disable.
enforce_admins.human_parameter_description: Choose whether these protection rules also apply to repository administrators.

allow_deletions.title: Allow Deletions
allow_deletions.description: Allows deletion of the protected branch.
allow_deletions.human_parameter_description: Allow the protected branch to be deleted. Keep off to prevent accidental deletions.

block_creations.title: Block Creations
block_creations.description: If `True`, push restrictions also apply to creating matching new branches, unless pusher has explicit push access.
block_creations.human_parameter_description: Also block the creation of new branches that match this rule unless the creator has push access. Use this to stop unauthorized branch creation.

allow_force_pushes.title: Allow Force Pushes
allow_force_pushes.description: Permits force pushes to the protected branch. Set to `True` to allow, `None`/`null` to block.
allow_force_pushes.human_parameter_description: Allow people to force push to the protected branch. Only enable this if you truly need to rewrite history.

allow_fork_syncing.title: Allow Fork Syncing
allow_fork_syncing.description: Allows users to pull upstream changes into their fork when the branch is locked.
allow_fork_syncing.human_parameter_description: Allow users to pull upstream changes into their forks even when the branch is locked. Helps keep forks up to date.

restrictions__apps.title: Restrictions  Apps
restrictions__apps.description: App `slug`s with push access. Cannot be used with `restrictions_users` or `restrictions_teams`. Empty list removes all.
restrictions__apps.human_parameter_description: Apps that are allowed to push directly to the protected branch. Leave empty to remove all app exceptions.

restrictions__teams.title: Restrictions  Teams
restrictions__teams.description: Team `slug`s with push access. Cannot be used with `restrictions_apps` or `restrictions_users`. Empty list removes all.
restrictions__teams.human_parameter_description: Team slugs that are allowed to push directly to the protected branch. Leave empty to remove all team exceptions.

restrictions__users.title: Restrictions  Users
restrictions__users.description: User `login`s with push access. Cannot be used with `restrictions_apps` or `restrictions_teams`. Empty list removes all.
restrictions__users.human_parameter_description: Usernames who are allowed to push directly to the protected branch. Leave empty to remove all user exceptions.

required_linear_history.title: Required Linear History
required_linear_history.description: Enforces linear commit history by preventing merge commits. Repository must allow squash or rebase merging.
required_linear_history.human_parameter_description: Prevent merge commits so the branch history stays linear. Use this to enforce squash or rebase workflows.

items.title: StatusCheck

app_id.description: The optional ID of the GitHub App that must provide this check.

context.title: Context
context.description: The name of the required status check.

items.description: Model for a status check requirement.

required__status__checks__checks.title: Required  Status  Checks  Checks
required__status__checks__checks.description: List of status checks required to merge. Each check object needs a `context` string and optionally an `app_id` integer. **Mutually exclusive with `contexts`** - use one or the other, not both.
required__status__checks__checks.human_parameter_description: Use this to list the specific status checks that must pass before merging. Include the check name (context) and optionally the app that runs it.

required__status__checks__strict.title: Required  Status  Checks  Strict
required__status__checks__strict.description: Require branches to be up to date with the base branch before merging; if `True`, merges are blocked if the head branch is behind the base branch.
required__status__checks__strict.human_parameter_description: Choose whether the branch must be fully up to date with the base branch before it can be merged. Turn this on to prevent merging when the branch is behind.

required_conversation_resolution.title: Required Conversation Resolution

required_conversation_resolution.human_parameter_description: Require all review discussions to be resolved before merging. Ensures feedback is addressed before changes go in.

required__status__checks__contexts.title: Required  Status  Checks  Contexts
required__status__checks__contexts.description: **Deprecated**: List of status check contexts required to merge. If set by a GitHub App, future checks must come from that app. Use `checks` for finer control. **Mutually exclusive with `checks`** - use one or the other, not both.
required__status__checks__contexts.human_parameter_description: Names of the status checks that must pass before merging (for example, your CI or lint jobs).

required__pull__request__reviews__dismis.title: Required  Pull  Request  Reviews  Dismiss  Stale  Reviews
required__pull__request__reviews__dismis.description: If `True`, new commits dismiss previous review approvals on a pull request branch.
required__pull__request__reviews__dismis.human_parameter_description: Automatically dismiss approvals when new commits are pushed so reviewers must re-approve the latest changes.

required__pull_request__reviews__approvi.description: Number of approving reviews (0-6) required to merge a pull request; 0 disables.
required__pull_request__reviews__approvi.human_parameter_description: How many approving reviews are required before merging. Set to 0 to disable the approval requirement.

required__pull_request__reviews__bypass_.description: App `slug`s allowed to bypass pull request requirements. Empty list removes all.
required__pull_request__reviews__bypass_.human_parameter_name: Apps allowed to bypass pull request requirements
required__pull_request__reviews__bypass_.human_parameter_description: Apps that may bypass pull request requirements. Grant only to trusted automation.

required__pull_request__reviews__bypass_.description: Team `slug`s allowed to bypass pull request requirements. Empty list removes all.

required__pull_request__reviews__bypass_.human_parameter_description: Team slugs allowed to merge without meeting all pull request requirements. Use for trusted teams.

required__pull_request__reviews__dismiss.title: Required  Pull Request  Reviews  Dismiss  Restrictions  Apps
required__pull_request__reviews__dismiss.description: App `slug`s allowed to dismiss pull request reviews. Empty list removes all.
required__pull_request__reviews__dismiss.human_parameter_description: App slugs that are allowed to dismiss pull request reviews. Useful for approved automation tools.

required__pull_request__reviews__dismiss.title: Required  Pull Request  Reviews  Dismiss  Restrictions  Teams
required__pull_request__reviews__dismiss.description: Team `slug`s allowed to dismiss pull request reviews. Empty list removes all.
required__pull_request__reviews__dismiss.human_parameter_description: Team slugs who are allowed to dismiss pull request reviews. Use this to grant override ability to trusted teams.

required__pull_request__reviews__dismiss.title: Required  Pull Request  Reviews  Dismiss  Restrictions  Users
required__pull_request__reviews__dismiss.description: User `login`s allowed to dismiss pull request reviews. Empty list removes all.
required__pull_request__reviews__dismiss.human_parameter_description: Usernames who are allowed to dismiss pull request reviews. Add trusted people who can override reviews when needed.

required__pull_request__reviews__require.title: Required  Pull Request  Reviews  Require  Code  Owner  Reviews

required__pull_request__reviews__require.human_parameter_description: Require approval from code owners when their files are changed. Ensures the right people review sensitive areas.

required__pull_request__reviews__require.title: Required  Pull Request  Reviews  Require  Last  Push  Approval
